findings.description: The new RegatePlan type keeps the nested `regate: { head, prUrl }` object, which only made sense when it was an optional field on every PullRequestPlan. It is now required and already implied by the type, so callers read the stutter `pullRequest.regate.head`/`.prUrl` (regateMerged lines 160, 177, 205-208, 215-221). `regate.prUrl` also always equals `adoptedUrl`, because planRegate refuses when they differ (line 129). A flat `head` field on RegatePlan, with `adoptedUrl` (or a `prUrl` field in its place), would express the contract directly.

The decision 86 amendment says the four functions "moved there unchanged", but the same paragraph says `planRegate` now returns `RegatePlan` and `regateMerged` takes the plan alone, and the code matches that. Drop "unchanged" or qualify it, e.g. "moved there, with `planRegate` now returning `RegatePlan`".

The decision 86 amendment's last sentence covers test-helper refactors (`expectRefusedUnwritten`, "one teardown helper"). That is test-file bookkeeping, not a decision, so it will go stale when the tests change, and the helper's actual name is `dropReviewBranch`. Drop the sentence and keep "No behaviour changed".
